summary:
Round 1, tests. The two recorded reds were RE-RUN, not read, and both reproduce on this tree. (a) SubscriptionHub:409 `coldMode(serving, targets.size())` -> `coldMode(serving, 1)`: ThreeModesAgreeTest reports tests=2 failures=1. (b) ConsumerClient.bytesOf's `if (delivery.via() != FetchMode.DIRECT)` -> `if (true)` (never fetch, always return the carried array): tests=2 failures=1. The tree was restored and :http:test :ingest:test :client:test re-run green afterwards; `git status --short` is the three staged files and `git diff` is empty.

CAN ALL THREE COLLAPSE? NO, and this is the question the row turns on. `recordsThrough` ends with `assertThat(bridge.modesSeen).isNotEmpty().containsOnly(expected)` where `modesSeen` holds `push.via()` -- the SAME field the bridge copies into `Delivery` and the same field `bytesOf` branches on, so it is the mode the consumer was told rather than the mode the policy computed. The three configs genuinely reach three arms: INLINE by size with heldBytes (FetchPolicy:97 `batchBytes <= inlineBound`), PROXY cold through `streamFromStore` with a real store read, DIRECT cold at fan-out 1 against threshold 4. And the values are pinned absolutely, not only relatively: `bodies(inline)` is `containsExactly("500:a:...","501:b:...","502:c:...")` and proxy and direct are `isEqualTo(bodies(inline))`, so a mode serving the same wrong records everywhere still reds.

IS THE BRIDGE HONEST ABOUT `direct`? YES, MEASURED. Mutation (b) is the proof: forcing `bytesOf` to return `delivery.segment()` fails the direct case, which means the array the HubBridge hands over is NOT decodable. It is the zero-length array `AssemblingSubscriber.complete` builds because `SubscriptionHub`'s DIRECT arm passes `sinks -> { }`, so the bridge gives the consumer nothing production would not give it, and the fetch is genuinely load-bearing. The bridge also carries `push.grant()` rather than the six-argument constructor, so `AssemblingSubscriber`'s grant-drop defect stays pinned from this side too.

CRITERION 2 is not vacuous: `neverCalled` throws an AssertionError (an Error, which `decodeInto`'s IOException catch does not swallow) and `modesSeen` is asserted non-empty and DIRECT-free, so both a served DIRECT and a delivered-nothing run red. The `<=` boundary in `FetchPolicy.wantsDirect` that this case does not pin is pinned by FetchPolicyTest:94 `theFANOUTDialStillDecidesOnceTheDeploymentHasEnabledTheMode` ("at the threshold, direct"), and the cold-INLINE correction it also does not pin is pinned by DirectServingTest:111 -- so neither is a gap, and I am not reporting them as findings.

No existing assertion was touched or weakened: the staged diff is one new test class, one test-only Gradle dependency, and one backlog cell. Criterion 3 is a gate (check-module PASSED in the packet), correctly not re-asserted as a test. The two findings below are minor and both are held elsewhere in the tree; neither blocks.

findings.title: The direct SegmentSource strips a fixed url prefix, so it serves any url ending in the right key rather than one exact url -- an UNSIGNED grant decodes fine here
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, RUN not reasoned: replace the body of GrantIssuer.grantFor(String, Duration)'s try block with `return new SignedUrl("https://store.example/" + segmentKey, Instant.EPOCH.plus(ttl));` -- i.e. an issuer that NEVER CALLS store.presign at all and hands the consumer an unsigned url. ThreeModesAgreeTest reports tests=2 skipped=0 failures=0 errors=0. It passes because the source does `store.get(grant.url().substring("https://store.example/".length()))`, so anything whose suffix is SEGMENT_KEY resolves, whereas DirectFetchTest's `ServesOneUrl` throws for any url but one. THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN M5.45g CRITERION 4 AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: DirectFetchTest is untouched by this diff, `theSEAMIsHandedTheGrantFromTheDELIVERY` still holds the exact-url binding client-side with its two-delivery memoization case, and the same mutation is killed ingester-side by GrantIssuerTest, DirectServingTest and GrantNeverLoggedTest (I ran :ingest:test under it and those three are the failing classes). So the binding is held, just not here -- and M5.45e's criteria (1)(2)(3) do not ask for it. Worth one line of javadoc in this file saying the url binding lives in DirectFetchTest, because the next reader of a test named 'all three modes agree' will reasonably assume this fixture is the strict one. A backlog note at most, not a change to this commit.
findings.mutation: GrantIssuer.grantFor: bypass store.presign and construct the url from segmentKey -- both cases stay green

findings.title: `bodies()` projects offset, id and payload only, so three decoded fields are compared by neither the absolute assertion nor the cross-mode one
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION: ConsumerClient.decodeInto:91 `long createdAt = reader.createdAtMillis();` -> `long createdAt = 0L;`. Both cases stay green, because `ConsumerRecord.createdAt()` never reaches the projection. `OpType` and the record's version (`OptionalLong`) are in the same position -- SegmentReader decodes them and the string `offset + ":" + id + ":" + payload` drops them. The cross-mode comparison cannot backstop this by construction: all three modes run the SAME `ConsumerClient.decodeInto`, so any field the projection drops is dropped identically in all three and `bodies(direct).isEqualTo(bodies(inline))` holds regardless; only the `containsExactly` literal could see it, and it does not. The projection exists for a real reason -- `SegmentRecord` holds a `byte[]`, so record equals() is reference identity and `isEqualTo` on the lists would be wrong -- so the fix is to widen the projection (`+ ":" + r.record().opType() + ":" + r.record().version()`), not to change the comparison. Held elsewhere: createdAt is asserted through plugin EndToEndTest, and opType/version by the format module's golden segment cases, which is why this is minor rather than major; the residue is that a test named for byte-identical RECORDS compares three of a record's five fields.
findings.mutation: ConsumerClient.decodeInto: createdAtMillis() -> 0L -- both cases stay green
